cases.name: empty object
cases.why: no order, no hidden → canonical

cases.name: empty array
cases.why: typeof [] is 'object' and it is truthy, so it is NOT the early-return default; it reaches the reconcile loop with no order

cases.name: null
cases.why: falsy → default

cases.name: string
cases.why: typeof 'string' → default

cases.name: number
cases.why: typeof 'number' → default

cases.name: true
cases.why: typeof 'boolean' → default

cases.name: non-array order and hidden
cases.why: Array.isArray gates both; a string is treated as absent

cases.name: minimal preset with one more hidden card
cases.why: a single extra hidden first-class card breaks the match

cases.name: the read-parity fixture blob
cases.why: unknown ids, a non-string, a duplicate, a callout in hidden and an unknown in hidden — all in one row

cases.name: order holds only hero
cases.why: task_list has no preceding canonical neighbour, so it is UNSHIFTed to the front, and every later card chains after it — hero ends up second, not first

cases.name: order holds only the last canonical card
cases.why: everything slots in before it via the neighbour chain

cases.name: order reversed
cases.why: known ids keep the user's order; nothing is missing so nothing is slotted

cases.name: canonical minus the first card
cases.why: the missing card is the one with no preceding neighbour → unshift

cases.name: canonical minus hero, hero hidden
cases.why: a hidden card that is also missing from order is slotted back in AND stays hidden

cases.name: two cards, callouts in hidden
cases.why: callouts are dropped from hidden entirely — it comes back empty

cases.name: wrong version and an extra key
cases.why: v is forced to 1 and unknown keys vanish

cases.name: non-string junk in both arrays
cases.why: typeof id === 'string' filters before the set lookup

cases.name: watchdog order truncated to five
cases.why: the rest is slotted by neighbour; whether that still matches the preset is for Node to say

cases.name: hidden duplicated and unsorted
cases.why: dedupe then canonical sort

cases.name: override: parent off
cases.why: step 6 — every dependent of an off parent collapses to off, with override null on the dependents

cases.name: override: parent off, child on
cases.why: step 7 — the child's own override beats the dependency collapse; its focusValue (override stripped) stays off

cases.name: override: kill switch off with other overrides
cases.why: every flag is its hard default — INCLUDING the kill switch's own row, whose currentValue ignores its override, and including the overridden ones

cases.name: override: kill switch on explicitly
cases.why: an override equal to the hard default is a no-op for values but still reported as an override

cases.name: override: parent set to a value that is not on/off
cases.why: override_value is an unchecked cast — it is echoed verbatim, and `parentValue !== 'on'` still collapses the dependents

cases.name: override: override equal to the resolved value
cases.why: override non-null, currentValue === focusValue

cases.name: override: unknown key
cases.why: getAllOverrides drops keys the registry does not know, so nothing changes and no row carries it

cases.name: override: quarantined-looking value on the desktop flag under web runtime
cases.why: the runtime rule (step 5) runs BEFORE the override (step 7), so an override off wins over the forced on

cases.name: audience is not one of the three
cases.why: AUDIENCE_RULES[audience] is undefined and indexing it throws — the route answers 500 {error:'Failed to list flags'}

cases.name: audience is an Object.prototype property name
cases.why: AUDIENCE_RULES['constructor'] is a FUNCTION, not undefined, so the lookup does not throw and no audience rule applies

cases.name: override: grandparent off
cases.why: flag.detail.policy.run_log_details → flag.detail.policy.run_log_strip → flag.detail.policy.panel: the collapse recurses through two levels
